links.outcome: Whether physician review of LLM drafts removed the confabulation before finalizing notes
links.effect: The single confabulation in 50 LLM drafts was removed in 5 of 6 LLM-assisted notes; the least-experienced physician missed it. Physician editing improved conciseness but slightly lowered completeness and correctness scores versus drafts.
links.quote: The single confabulation documented unperformed procedures (splint application, dressing) and was removed in 5 of 6 LLM-assisted notes—by all except the least-experienced physician—indicating that brief clinician review remains necessary despite high baseline quality.

links.outcome: Note quality and writing time for physicians with versus without LLM assistance
links.effect: LLM-assisted notes scored higher than manual notes on all 4C metrics (all P<.001); median writing time fell from 69.5 to 32.0 seconds.
links.quote: The median documentation time per note dropped from 69.5 (95% CI, 65.5-78.0) seconds for manual notes to 32.0 (95% CI, 29.5-36.0) seconds for LLM-assisted notes (P < .001).

links.quote: In a targeted audit of the 50 LLM drafts, 6 omission cases and 1 confabulation case were identified (examples summarized in eTable 8 in Supplement 1 ).
